messages.subject: Unconventional library loading with apply will not work for deployment (package not found)
messages.subject_clean: Unconventional library loading with apply will not work for deployment (package not found)
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

I just thought I'd make a post here, even though it is not a question, but in case other have similar issues in the future.

I have, lately, taken to loading multiple packages using sapply.

example:
> LIBS=c("rio","rmarkdown","tidyverse","plotly","png","svglite")
> sapply(LIBS, library, character.only=T)

Of course, this works perfectly locally, but not when deploying the app to shinyapp.io <http://shinyapp.io>. When initiating on the server, it would throw errors about the packages not being installed. It tok me so long to understand what was going on, initially thinking I had not installed the packages in the "correct" way, and was going round in circles trying to fix the issue.

In the end, I found this post: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/88
and understood what was going on. I had not understood the search the deployment does to find the packages necessary for the app to run. Since it specifically searches for string calls to library() or require(), wrapping them in an apply obviously would not provide any results.

so, in case other have started loading libraries in this new an peculiar way: it wont work for your shinyApp deployment!

messages.subject_clean: Unconventional library loading with apply will not work for deployment (package not found)
messages.body_plain:
There are some articles about dependency packages for shiny server that explained the requirement.

I've been using pacman because I want my app to install missing packages automatically in local mode. Usually you must install all the packages before running the app, with pacman you can run the app, and the packages will be installed if missing.

So I have

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(shiny, shinydashboard, DT,
               markdown, crayon, rmarkdown, knitr,
               ctmm, data.table, parallel,
               ggplot2, scales, grid, gridExtra, lubridate,
               httr, stringr, XML, xml2, zip)

Imagine how many library calls I need for this, and how many libraries I need to ask user to install before running the app...

The pacman usage doesn't work in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> for similar reasons. I created a PR for packrat (which is the underlying mechanism used by shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) to support the usage, but they don't want to merge it as official.

If this feature (or install missing packages automatically) is useful for you, you can download my fork <https://github.com/xhdong-umd/packrat>, install the package locally, then you can use pacman in your app.

I have an app with two Rmd files run by shiny that I'd like people to be able to click between. Call them a.Rmd and b.Rmd.

https://blah.shinyapps.io/app/_w_f974a5b7/b.Rmd.

This works fine, until I try to click back to a.Rmd from b.Rmd. Then, the URL becomes

https://blah.shinyapps.io/app/_w_f974a5b7/_w_f974a5b7/a.Rmd.

because the base href is added on a second time. This link fails with an internal server error.

Of course, this is easy to get around by constructing absolute URLs, but I was wondering what the purpose of the base href is in this case? Does it keep the server from starting new instances? Does it keep track of users?

Is there any way to work around this with relative URLs?

Is there any drawback to working around this with absolute URLs? (e.g., more simultaneous sessions are created)

Thanks,
Richard

messages.body_plain:
I wrote a simple shiny app to illustrate a problem I am having fetching data from a website. Here is the UI code:

    library(shiny)

    shinyUI(fluidPage(

    # Application title
    titlePanel("Test App"),

    # Sidebar with slider inputs
    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
            actionButton("button", "Fetch Data")
                    ),

        mainPanel(
            tabsetPanel(
                tabPanel("Data", textOutput("crimelist"))
            )
        )
      )
     )
    )

And here is the Server code:

    library(shiny)

    # Define server logic
    shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

        # Get a list of the different types of crime
        observeEvent(input$button, {
            url <- "https://phl.carto.com/api/v2/sql?format=csv&q=SELECT
                   distinct rtrim(text_general_code) as text_general_code
                                FROM incidents_part1_part2
                                order by text_general_code"
        crimelist <- read.csv(url(url), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$text_general_code
        output$crimelist <- renderText({crimelist})
        })
    })

The data being fetched is described at https://cityofphiladelphia.github.io/carto-api-explorer/#incidents_part1_part2.

When I run this shiny app in my local environment, it works perfectly. When publish it to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and run it, the application fails when I click the button to fetch the data. In the shiny log, it reports the following:

    2017-10-11T14:46:31.242058+00:00 shinyapps[224106]: Warning in
    open.connection(file, "rt") :
    2017-10-11T14:46:31.242061+00:00 shinyapps[224106]:   URL 'https://phl.carto.com/api/v2/sql?format=csv&q=SELECT distinct

    2017-10-11T14:46:31.243062+00:00 shinyapps[224106]: Warning: Error in open.connection: cannot open connection

I am really stumped - is this a shiny server issue of some kind? If anyone out there has a clue, I am all ears!

messages.body_plain:
You need to encode the URL in order for it to be valid, e.g. https://phl.carto.com/api/v2/sql?format=csv&q= <https://www.google.com/url?q=https%3A%2F%2Fphl.carto.com%2Fapi%2Fv2%2Fsql%3Fformat%3Dcsv%26q%3DSELECT&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNEZNxvMEUXO2ZWu47sZc753DVaEOw>SELECT%20distinct%20rtrim(text_general_code)%20as%20text_general_code%20FROM%20incidents_part1_part2%20order%20by%20text_general_code

shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> runs on Linux, so it is likely that curl is being used to fetch this URL. My guess is that you are using Windows locally, which uses a less strict mechanism that is tolerant of the spaces and newlines you have in the URL.

Hi everyone.

We are implementing a set of dashboards for a client and I am trying to understand what the best tool would be for it.
They don't have a massive budget, so a BI tool is not an option.

My options would be Plotly Dash and Shiny, but I would probably prefer Shiny because I used it several times before. I would go with the professional plan and embed it to our client's portal.

My questions deploying the dashboard on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> would be:
- can I set rights on what people can see? e.g. tab-level view permissions?
- can I set up an unlimited number of users (consumers, not devs)?
- I can see that one account can be shared with many developers, however, can you set up developers per dashboard?

Many thanks for the help!

Ana
